title: Cross-SDK resilience blueprint: adaptive backoff, id-key handshake, and stream-resume ergonomics
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Goal: Define and implement a unified, practical resilience blueprint for Python/TypeScript/Go SDKs that balances cost, latency, and correctness. Deliverables include: (1) adaptive backoff profiles tuned for token/cost budgets and latency tiers, (2) an interoperable idempotency key (id-key) handshake and header conventions for safe retries and deduplication across transports, and (3) ergonomic stream-resume primitives with explicit resume tokens and safety windows. This ticket covers spec, reference implementations, tests, and migration notes.
acceptance_criteria: Spec doc published and reviewed by SDK, Runtime, and Product teams
Reference implementations in python-sdk, ts-sdk, and go-sdk with feature flags
End-to-end integration tests exercising retry flows, id-key negotiation, and stream-resume across client+runtime
Telemetry hooks emitting retry_reason, idkey_fingerprint, resume_token_usage, and retry_budget_consumed
Migration guide for existing SDK users with examples and opt-in compatibility mode
implementation_notes: Backoff profiles: define three presets: conservative (P2-like), balanced (default), and aggressive (latency-first). Each preset is an algorithm: base_delay + jitter, capped by token_cost_budget and per-call latency target. Example formula: delay = min(max_backoff, base * 2^attempt) * U(0.8,1.2), but reduce multiplier when response tokens > token_threshold.

Id-key handshake: introduce optional header X-Redwood-IdKey: <opaque-fingerprint> and X-Redwood-IdKey-Policy: hint ("allow-dup-suppression" | "weak" | "strong"). SDKs will generate id-keys using request fingerprint (api_key, model, prompt-hash, user-provided id) and optional time-window salt. Runtime will accept and return X-Redwood-IdKey-Ack when duplicate suppressed.

Streaming resume: provide resume_token in final stream message and an explicit server-returned resume_deadline. Client side keeps a small resume buffer keyed by id-key and resume_token; resume allowed only within resume_deadline and up to a capped token gap to avoid double-chaining large continuations.

Retryable error taxonomy: categorize errors into transient-network, transient-compute (GPU preemption, transient OOM), server-rate (capacity), model-decode (deterministic length mismatch), and user-input (validation). For each category define default retry policy and id-key behavior.

Per-language ergonomics: Python: context-manager wrapper with .retry_and_resume(), TypeScript: builder pattern with .withRetryProfile(), Go: functional options to configure backoff and id-key generation. All SDKs expose telemetry hooks for metrics described above.

Security: id-key fingerprinting avoids including PII; default fingerprint uses HMAC with client-side ephemeral salt stored only in memory. Document KMS/HSM integration if customers want server-side id-key signing.
